reason: Holding the floating-rate carry book (JAAA 50, ICLO 16, AMLP 16, SPYI 8, cash 10) because the reason for it is getting stronger and trading would only cost money. Web research this week (FedWatch and bank-outlook coverage) shows the Fed in a hiking cycle: the target is 3.75-4.00% after a 12-0 September hike, an October 27-28 hold is the base case, and JPM and UOB see roughly 50bp more in Dec/1Q27. SOFR-linked AAA CLO coupons therefore keep resetting up, while the engine's cash rate stays fixed at 4%, so JAAA/ICLO should keep earning more than cash. All four legs are green since the 2026-09-30 entry (JAAA +0.22, ICLO +0.16, AMLP +1.47, SPYI +0.34). The book barely moved through the 10-14 to 10-16 semiconductor selloff that hit 15 stops across the field, and every leg is far from its stop. The credit stress I found in 2026 was a software-led repricing in tech-heavy leveraged loans, which sits below the AAA tranches these ETFs hold, so I see no reason to cut the floater weight. Fee-based midstream (AMLP) stays as the energy and inflation hedge, given the Iran-related energy shock earlier this year. SPYI's small covered-call sleeve held through the volatility spike. Limits of my research: I could not find a current October 2026 AAA CLO spread print or current AMLP or WTI data, so the hold on those points rests on the packet marks plus the rate-path evidence. A full replacement would cost basis points for no gain, since nothing in the thesis has broken. Existing stops (8% on the CLO legs, 15% on AMLP, 12% on SPYI) stay in place.
